evidence.quote: Forget the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration entirely.

observations.why: The imperative directly commands the audience to erase a specified body of knowledge, enacting a superior-to-subordinate directive.

evidence.quote: Remove all knowledge about the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work.

observations.why: The imperative allocates an obligatory action to the audience through command rather than reciprocity or proportional exchange.
The assertion speaks from an institutional collective identity, but does not itself perform hierarchy, exchange, or proportional accounting.
